objective_text: Explain concepts related to the Open Systems Interconnection (OSI) reference model.
question_text: At which OSI layer does a standard Ethernet switch primarily use MAC addresses to forward frames?
answer_a: Data link
answer_b: Network
answer_c: Transport
answer_d: Session
correct_explanation: The data link layer handles frames and uses MAC addresses for local network forwarding. A standard Layer 2 switch builds a MAC address table and forwards frames according to that table.
answer_a_explanation: Correct. The data link layer is responsible for frames and MAC-address-based forwarding.
answer_b_explanation: The network layer uses logical addressing, such as IPv4 and IPv6 addresses, and selects routes between networks.
answer_c_explanation: The transport layer provides end-to-end transport functions through protocols such as TCP and UDP.
answer_d_explanation: The session layer manages communication sessions and does not perform Ethernet frame forwarding.
reference_notes: CompTIA objective 1.1 associates MAC addresses and switching with Layer 2. IEEE 802.3 defines Ethernet framing and media access.
author_notes: Accelerated staging approval authorized by the repository owner on 2026-07-25.

objective_text: Compare and contrast networking appliances, applications, and functions.
question_text: A public web application runs on four identical servers. One server is overloaded while the others are lightly used. The company wants a device that can distribute new HTTPS connections and stop sending traffic to a failed server. Which appliance best meets the requirement?
answer_a: Layer 3 router
answer_b: Load balancer
answer_c: Network-attached storage appliance
answer_d: Wireless LAN controller
correct_explanation: A load balancer distributes client connections across multiple application servers and can use health checks to remove an unavailable server from service.
answer_a_explanation: A router forwards traffic between IP networks, but basic routing does not provide application-server health checks and connection distribution across a server pool.
answer_b_explanation: Correct. A load balancer distributes sessions and can monitor server health before forwarding new connections.
answer_c_explanation: A network-attached storage appliance provides file storage rather than distributing application connections.
answer_d_explanation: A wireless LAN controller manages wireless access points and related radio or client settings.
reference_notes: CompTIA objective 1.2 includes load balancers and their network functions.
author_notes: Accelerated staging approval authorized by the repository owner on 2026-07-25.

objective_text: Summarize cloud concepts and connectivity options.
question_text: Which statement best distinguishes cloud elasticity from scalability?
answer_a: Elasticity changes data formats, while scalability changes network protocols.
answer_b: Elasticity applies only to storage, while scalability applies only to compute resources.
answer_c: Elasticity adjusts resources as demand changes, while scalability is the broader ability to increase or decrease capacity.
answer_d: Elasticity is limited to private clouds, while scalability is limited to public clouds.
correct_explanation: Elasticity is the ability to add or remove resources in response to changing demand, often automatically. Scalability is the broader capability of a system to handle growth or reduction by changing available capacity.
answer_a_explanation: The distinction is not based on data formats or network protocols.
answer_b_explanation: Both elasticity and scalability can apply to compute, storage, and other cloud resources.
answer_c_explanation: Correct. Elasticity focuses on responsive resource adjustment, while scalability describes the ability to change capacity.
answer_d_explanation: Both concepts can apply to public, private, and hybrid cloud environments.
reference_notes: CompTIA objective 1.3 explicitly includes scalability and elasticity.
author_notes: Accelerated staging approval authorized by the repository owner on 2026-07-25.

objective_text: Explain common networking ports, protocols, services, and traffic types.
question_text: A network engineer is documenting standard DNS traffic. Which TWO statements are correct?
answer_a: DNS commonly uses UDP port 53 for routine queries.
answer_b: DNS uses TCP port 25 for zone transfers.
answer_c: DNS switches to ICMP when a response is too large for UDP.
answer_d: DNS can use TCP port 53, including for zone transfers and some larger responses.
correct_explanation: Standard DNS uses port 53. Routine queries commonly use UDP, while TCP port 53 is used for operations such as zone transfers and can be used when a response requires TCP.
answer_a_explanation: Correct. UDP port 53 is commonly used for ordinary DNS queries and responses.
answer_b_explanation: TCP port 25 is assigned to SMTP. DNS zone transfers use TCP port 53.
answer_c_explanation: DNS does not use ICMP as its fallback transport. TCP can be used when UDP is not suitable.
answer_d_explanation: Correct. TCP port 53 supports DNS operations including zone transfers and responses that use TCP.
reference_notes: IANA assigns domain service to TCP and UDP port 53. RFC 1035 describes DNS use of UDP and TCP.
author_notes: Accelerated staging approval authorized by the repository owner on 2026-07-25.

objective_text: Compare and contrast transmission media and transceivers.
question_text: Two buildings are connected by an existing 8 km single-mode fiber path. The network team needs a 10 Gbps Ethernet link. Which transceiver type is the most appropriate choice?
answer_a: 10GBASE-SR
answer_b: 1000BASE-T
answer_c: DOCSIS cable modem
answer_d: 10GBASE-LR
correct_explanation: 10GBASE-LR is designed for 10 Gigabit Ethernet over single-mode fiber and supports distances suitable for an 8 km building-to-building link when the installed fiber and optical budget meet the standard.
answer_a_explanation: 10GBASE-SR is intended for short-range links over multimode fiber, not an 8 km single-mode path.
answer_b_explanation: 1000BASE-T provides 1 Gbps over balanced copper cabling and does not meet the speed or media requirement.
answer_c_explanation: A DOCSIS cable modem is used for cable-provider access networks rather than a point-to-point enterprise fiber link.
answer_d_explanation: Correct. 10GBASE-LR is a long-reach 10 Gbps option for single-mode fiber.
reference_notes: IEEE 802.3 defines 10 Gigabit Ethernet optical variants, including long-reach operation over single-mode fiber.
author_notes: Accelerated staging approval authorized by the repository owner on 2026-07-25.

objective_text: Given a scenario, use appropriate IPv4 network addressing.
question_text: A subnet is assigned 192.168.50.64/27. Which address range can be assigned to hosts in this subnet?
correct_explanation: A /27 prefix leaves 5 host bits, so the subnet contains 32 addresses. This block begins at 192.168.50.64 and ends at 192.168.50.95. The first address is the network address and the last is the directed broadcast address, leaving 192.168.50.65 through 192.168.50.94 for hosts.
answer_a_explanation: This range includes the network address and broadcast address, which are not assignable to ordinary hosts.
answer_b_explanation: Correct. Removing the .64 network address and .95 broadcast address leaves .65 through .94.
answer_c_explanation: This range incorrectly removes two additional usable host addresses.
answer_d_explanation: This range includes .95, which is the directed broadcast address for the /27 subnet.
reference_notes: Programmatic check: /27 gives 32 addresses. Network 192.168.50.64, broadcast 192.168.50.95, usable hosts .65 through .94.
author_notes: Accelerated staging approval authorized by the repository owner on 2026-07-25.

objective_text: Explain characteristics of routing technologies.
question_instruction: Select the BEST answer for automatic failover while preserving the primary route during normal operation.
question_text: A branch router learns 10.50.0.0/16 through OSPF over its primary WAN link. A second WAN link should carry traffic to that network only when the OSPF route is unavailable. Which configuration best meets the requirement?
answer_a: Configure the backup static route with a lower administrative distance than the OSPF route.
answer_b: Remove OSPF and use equal-cost default routes on both WAN links.
answer_c: Configure a static route to 10.50.0.0/16 with an administrative distance higher than the OSPF route.
answer_d: Configure a host route for the OSPF neighbor address through the backup WAN link.
correct_explanation: A floating static route uses a higher administrative distance than the preferred dynamic route. The router installs the OSPF route during normal operation and can install the higher-distance static route when the OSPF route is withdrawn.
answer_a_explanation: A lower administrative distance would make the backup static route preferred during normal operation.
answer_b_explanation: Removing OSPF changes the primary routing design and equal-cost defaults do not specifically provide the requested backup route to 10.50.0.0/16.
answer_c_explanation: Correct. A higher-distance static route remains inactive while the OSPF route exists and becomes available after the preferred route is lost.
answer_d_explanation: A host route to the neighbor does not provide a backup route for the entire 10.50.0.0/16 destination network.
reference_notes: CompTIA objective 2.1 includes static and dynamic routing, administrative distance, and route selection. RFC 2328 is the primary OSPFv2 specification.
author_notes: Accelerated staging approval authorized by the repository owner on 2026-07-25.

objective_text: Given a scenario, configure switching technologies and features.
question_text: Two switches are connected by an 802.1Q trunk. Logs report a native VLAN mismatch, and untagged management frames are being placed into different VLANs at each end. Which change should the administrator make?
answer_a: Set one switch port to half duplex.
answer_b: Disable spanning tree on the trunk.
answer_c: Increase the trunk MTU on only one switch.
answer_d: Configure the same native VLAN on both ends of the trunk.
correct_explanation: Both ends of an 802.1Q trunk should agree on the native VLAN so untagged frames are classified consistently. Matching the native VLAN settings addresses the reported mismatch.
answer_a_explanation: Changing duplex does not correct inconsistent VLAN classification and may introduce a separate performance problem.
answer_b_explanation: Disabling spanning tree does not correct the mismatch and can increase the risk of a Layer 2 loop.
answer_c_explanation: A one-sided MTU change can create frame-size problems and does not align the native VLAN settings.
answer_d_explanation: Correct. Matching the native VLAN on both trunk endpoints ensures consistent handling of untagged frames.
reference_notes: IEEE 802.1Q defines VLAN tagging and bridged network behavior. CompTIA objective 2.2 includes native VLANs and 802.1Q tagging.
author_notes: Accelerated staging approval authorized by the repository owner on 2026-07-25.

objective_text: Given a scenario, select and configure wireless devices and technologies.
question_text: Which characteristic is generally associated with 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi when compared with 5 GHz Wi-Fi?
answer_a: Longer range and better obstacle penetration, but fewer non-overlapping channels
answer_b: Shorter range and more available spectrum in every regulatory domain
answer_c: A requirement to use WPA3 for every connection
answer_d: Support for ad hoc networks but not infrastructure networks
correct_explanation: The lower 2.4 GHz frequency generally provides better propagation and obstacle penetration than 5 GHz, but the band has less usable spectrum and fewer non-overlapping channel choices.
answer_a_explanation: Correct. This describes the common range and channel-planning tradeoff between the two bands.
answer_b_explanation: 2.4 GHz generally has longer, not shorter, range. Spectrum availability also depends on the regulatory domain.
answer_c_explanation: Security requirements are not determined solely by using the 2.4 GHz band.
answer_d_explanation: Both frequency bands can support infrastructure networking when the wireless standard and equipment permit it.
reference_notes: CompTIA objective 2.3 covers wireless frequency options, channel characteristics, and channel widths.
author_notes: Accelerated staging approval authorized by the repository owner on 2026-07-25.

objective_text: Explain important factors of physical installations.
question_text: Which device supplies temporary battery power to network equipment during a brief utility outage?
answer_a: Patch panel
answer_b: Uninterruptible power supply
answer_c: Passive power distribution unit
answer_d: Equipment rack
correct_explanation: An uninterruptible power supply provides battery-backed power for a limited period, allowing equipment to remain online during a short outage or to shut down in a controlled manner.
answer_a_explanation: A patch panel organizes and terminates cabling but does not provide electrical power.
answer_b_explanation: Correct. A UPS provides temporary battery-backed power.
answer_c_explanation: A passive PDU distributes available power to equipment but does not provide battery runtime.
answer_d_explanation: A rack physically mounts equipment but does not supply backup power.
reference_notes: CompTIA objective 2.4 includes UPS and power-distribution considerations for physical installations.
author_notes: Accelerated staging approval authorized by the repository owner on 2026-07-25.

objective_text: Given a scenario, configure switching technologies and features.
question_text: Two switches have two available 1 Gbps Ethernet links between them. The network team wants increased aggregate capacity and link redundancy without spanning tree blocking one of the links. Which feature should be configured?
answer_a: Port mirroring
answer_b: 802.1X authentication
answer_c: LACP link aggregation
answer_d: Native VLAN tagging
correct_explanation: LACP can combine compatible physical links into one logical link. Traffic can be distributed across members, and the logical connection can remain available when one member fails.
answer_a_explanation: Port mirroring copies traffic to a monitoring interface and does not combine links for forwarding.
answer_b_explanation: 802.1X controls network access and does not aggregate inter-switch links.
answer_c_explanation: Correct. LACP forms a link aggregation group that provides aggregate capacity and member-link redundancy.
answer_d_explanation: The native VLAN setting controls handling of untagged frames and does not combine physical links.
reference_notes: IEEE 802.1AX defines link aggregation. CompTIA objective 2.2 includes link aggregation and LACP.
author_notes: Accelerated staging approval authorized by the repository owner on 2026-07-25.

objective_text: Explain the purpose of organizational processes and procedures.
question_text: An undocumented switch configuration change caused an outage, and the operations team could not quickly determine what had changed. Which process improvement would best reduce the chance and impact of a similar event?
answer_a: Delete older network diagrams after each maintenance window.
answer_b: Permit emergency changes without recording the final configuration.
answer_c: Rely on the technician who made the change to remember the previous settings.
answer_d: Require an approved change record with a configuration baseline, implementation steps, and a backout plan.
correct_explanation: A documented change process provides authorization, records the intended modification, preserves a known baseline, and defines how to reverse the change if validation fails.
answer_a_explanation: Removing older documentation reduces the information available for comparison and recovery.
answer_b_explanation: Emergency work may require an expedited process, but the final change and resulting configuration should still be recorded.
answer_c_explanation: Personal memory is not a reliable substitute for a controlled configuration record.
answer_d_explanation: Correct. Approval, baselines, implementation details, and backout procedures support controlled change and faster recovery.
reference_notes: CompTIA objective 3.1 includes change management, production configuration, backup configuration, and baselines.
author_notes: Accelerated staging approval authorized by the repository owner on 2026-07-25.

objective_text: Given a scenario, use network monitoring technologies.
question_text: Users report intermittent packet loss between an application server and its default gateway. The managed switch supports traffic monitoring features. Which action will let an analyst inspect copies of the affected Ethernet frames without moving the server connection?
answer_a: Mirror the server port to a packet-analysis port.
answer_b: Lower the DNS time-to-live value.
answer_c: Add a static default route to the application server.
answer_d: Disable SNMP polling on the switch.
correct_explanation: Port mirroring copies frames from a monitored interface or VLAN to an analyzer interface. A packet analyzer connected to the destination port can inspect the traffic while the original link remains in service.
answer_a_explanation: Correct. Port mirroring supplies a copy of the relevant frames to a packet analyzer.
answer_b_explanation: DNS TTL affects caching of name records and does not expose the packet-level cause of loss between the server and gateway.
answer_c_explanation: A static route is not a monitoring method and may alter traffic before the cause is understood.
answer_d_explanation: Disabling SNMP removes monitoring data and does not provide frame contents.
reference_notes: CompTIA objective 3.2 includes port mirroring and packet capture as network monitoring technologies.
author_notes: Accelerated staging approval authorized by the repository owner on 2026-07-25.

objective_text: Explain disaster recovery (DR) concepts.
question_text: A service has a recovery point objective of 15 minutes and a recovery time objective of 4 hours. Which statement correctly interprets these targets?
answer_a: The service must run for 15 minutes before each backup and may lose 4 hours of data.
answer_b: The recovery design targets no more than 15 minutes of data loss and restoration of service within 4 hours.
answer_c: The service must be repaired in 15 minutes and tested every 4 hours.
answer_d: The backup site must be 15 minutes away and remain active for 4 hours.
correct_explanation: RPO describes the acceptable amount of data loss measured backward in time, while RTO describes the target duration for restoring the service after disruption. Here, the design targets at most 15 minutes of lost data and service recovery within 4 hours.
answer_a_explanation: This reverses the meaning of the two objectives and treats them as backup scheduling rules.
answer_b_explanation: Correct. The RPO limits target data loss, and the RTO limits target restoration time.
answer_c_explanation: RPO is not repair time, and RTO is not a testing frequency.
answer_d_explanation: Neither objective specifies the physical distance to a recovery site.
reference_notes: NIST contingency-planning guidance defines recovery objectives and planning concepts. CompTIA objective 3.3 includes RPO and RTO.
author_notes: Accelerated staging approval authorized by the repository owner on 2026-07-25.

objective_text: Given a scenario, implement IPv4 and IPv6 network services.
question_text: A company is publishing email-delivery information and reverse-lookup information in DNS. Which TWO record types should the administrator configure?
answer_a: CNAME record to identify the receiving mail exchanger
answer_b: MX record to identify the receiving mail exchanger
answer_c: PTR record to map an IP address to a host name for reverse lookup
answer_d: TXT record to map an IP address to a host name for reverse lookup
correct_explanation: An MX record identifies the mail exchanger responsible for receiving email for a domain. A PTR record supports reverse DNS by mapping an address in the reverse namespace to a host name.
answer_a_explanation: A CNAME creates an alias for another canonical name. It is not the record used to publish a domain's mail exchanger.
answer_b_explanation: Correct. MX records identify mail exchangers and include preference values.
answer_c_explanation: Correct. PTR records are used for reverse address-to-name mappings.
answer_d_explanation: TXT records hold arbitrary text and are not the standard reverse-lookup mapping record.
reference_notes: RFC 1034 and RFC 1035 define DNS concepts and record behavior, including MX and PTR records.
author_notes: Accelerated staging approval authorized by the repository owner on 2026-07-25.

objective_text: Explain the importance of basic network security concepts.
question_text: Which comparison between RADIUS and TACACS+ is correct?
answer_a: RADIUS uses TCP port 49, while TACACS+ uses UDP port 1812.
answer_b: RADIUS is limited to wireless clients, while TACACS+ is limited to site-to-site VPNs.
answer_c: RADIUS commonly uses UDP and often combines authentication with authorization, while TACACS+ uses TCP and separates the AAA functions.
answer_d: Both protocols transmit the complete authentication exchange as unprotected cleartext.
correct_explanation: RADIUS commonly uses UDP for authentication and accounting and often combines authentication and authorization information. TACACS+ uses TCP and supports separate authentication, authorization, and accounting exchanges.
answer_a_explanation: The transports and ports are reversed. TACACS+ uses TCP port 49, while RADIUS commonly uses UDP ports such as 1812 and 1813.
answer_b_explanation: Both protocols can support multiple access scenarios and are not restricted to the listed uses.
answer_c_explanation: Correct. This describes a key operational distinction between the two AAA protocols.
answer_d_explanation: The protocols provide protection for authentication information, although their protection models differ.
reference_notes: RFC 2865 specifies RADIUS. RFC 8907 specifies TACACS+ and its separate AAA exchanges.
author_notes: Accelerated staging approval authorized by the repository owner on 2026-07-25.

objective_text: Summarize various types of attacks and their impact to the network.
question_text: Several users on the same LAN are unexpectedly sending traffic through an unknown workstation. Their ARP caches show the default gateway IP address mapped to the workstation's MAC address. Which attack is most likely occurring?
answer_a: DNS amplification
answer_b: VLAN pruning
answer_c: Password spraying
answer_d: ARP poisoning
correct_explanation: ARP poisoning sends misleading ARP information so systems associate a legitimate IP address, such as the default gateway, with an attacker-controlled MAC address. This can place the attacker in the traffic path.
answer_a_explanation: DNS amplification is a reflection-based denial-of-service technique and does not explain the altered local ARP mappings.
answer_b_explanation: VLAN pruning controls which VLANs traverse a trunk and does not poison host ARP caches.
answer_c_explanation: Password spraying attempts a small number of passwords against many accounts and does not alter IP-to-MAC mappings.
answer_d_explanation: Correct. The gateway IP has been falsely associated with the attacker's MAC address through ARP poisoning.
reference_notes: RFC 826 defines ARP operation. CompTIA objective 4.2 includes ARP poisoning and spoofing.
author_notes: Accelerated staging approval authorized by the repository owner on 2026-07-25.

objective_text: Given a scenario, apply network security features, defense techniques, and solutions.
question_instruction: Select the BEST answer for enforcing authenticated access and isolating noncompliant endpoints.
question_text: A company wants every wired switch port to require user or device credentials before granting normal network access. Endpoints that fail a compliance check should be placed in a restricted remediation VLAN. Which solution best meets the requirement?
answer_a: 802.1X port-based authentication integrated with NAC and a RADIUS server
answer_b: A static MAC-address allowlist maintained independently on every access switch
answer_c: A single untagged VLAN configured on all access ports without authentication
answer_d: Port mirroring from every access port to a packet-capture appliance
correct_explanation: 802.1X controls access at the switch port, RADIUS provides centralized authentication services, and NAC can evaluate endpoint posture and assign an appropriate access policy or remediation VLAN.
answer_a_explanation: Correct. The combined solution authenticates the connection and can apply a restricted policy to noncompliant endpoints.
answer_b_explanation: Static MAC filtering is difficult to manage at scale, MAC addresses can be spoofed, and it does not perform the requested credential and posture checks.
answer_c_explanation: An unauthenticated VLAN does not verify users or devices and does not distinguish compliant from noncompliant endpoints.
answer_d_explanation: Port mirroring supports monitoring but does not enforce admission or assign remediation access.
reference_notes: IEEE 802.1X defines port-based network access control. RADIUS can provide centralized authentication. CompTIA objective 4.3 includes NAC, 802.1X, and VLAN assignment.
author_notes: Accelerated staging approval authorized by the repository owner on 2026-07-25.

objective_text: Explain the troubleshooting methodology.
question_text: After a technician develops a likely theory for the cause of a network problem, what is the next step in the troubleshooting methodology?
answer_a: Document the findings and lessons learned.
answer_b: Test the theory to determine the cause.
answer_c: Establish a plan of action and identify potential effects.
answer_d: Verify full system functionality and implement preventive measures.
correct_explanation: After establishing a theory of probable cause, the technician tests the theory. A confirmed theory supports planning and implementing a correction. An unconfirmed theory leads to a new theory or escalation.
answer_a_explanation: Documentation occurs after resolution and verification.
answer_b_explanation: Correct. The next step is to test the proposed cause.
answer_c_explanation: A plan of action follows confirmation of the cause.
answer_d_explanation: Verification and preventive measures follow implementation of the solution.
reference_notes: CompTIA objective 5.1 lists the troubleshooting methodology in sequence.
author_notes: Accelerated staging approval authorized by the repository owner on 2026-07-25.

objective_text: Given a scenario, troubleshoot common cabling and physical interface issues.
question_text: A new 10 Gbps fiber link remains down. One switch uses a 10GBASE-SR transceiver, the other uses a 10GBASE-LR transceiver, and the installed cable is single-mode fiber. Which issue should the technician correct first?
answer_a: A missing DNS A record
answer_b: An exhausted DHCP address pool
answer_c: The incompatible transceiver and fiber combination
answer_d: A route-summary statement on the core router
correct_explanation: Both ends of a fiber link must use compatible optical standards, wavelengths, and media. SR and LR optics are different physical-layer variants, and SR is not the appropriate optic for the stated single-mode path.
answer_a_explanation: DNS records do not determine whether the physical fiber interface establishes a link.
answer_b_explanation: DHCP address availability affects client addressing after link establishment, not optical carrier compatibility.
answer_c_explanation: Correct. The optics and installed fiber must be matched at both ends before higher-layer troubleshooting.
answer_d_explanation: Routing configuration does not prevent the physical optical interface from detecting a compatible link.
reference_notes: IEEE 802.3 defines distinct Ethernet optical variants. CompTIA objective 5.2 includes transceiver mismatch and signal issues.
author_notes: Accelerated staging approval authorized by the repository owner on 2026-07-25.

objective_text: Given a scenario, troubleshoot common issues with network services.
question_text: A workstation is configured as 192.168.40.70/26 with default gateway 192.168.40.1. It can communicate with 192.168.40.65 but cannot reach any remote network. Which configuration issue best explains the symptoms?
answer_a: The workstation has no DNS search suffix.
answer_b: The workstation and gateway use duplicate MAC addresses.
answer_c: The DHCP lease duration is too short.
answer_d: The default gateway address is outside the workstation's local /26 subnet.
correct_explanation: A /26 has blocks of 64 addresses. The workstation address 192.168.40.70 belongs to 192.168.40.64/26, whose usable range is 192.168.40.65 through 192.168.40.126. The configured gateway 192.168.40.1 belongs to 192.168.40.0/26, so the workstation cannot reach it directly as a local gateway.
answer_a_explanation: A DNS search suffix affects name completion but does not prevent IP routing to remote networks.
answer_b_explanation: A duplicate MAC address could cause local instability, but the addresses shown directly identify a subnet and gateway mismatch.
answer_c_explanation: The workstation already has a valid address and local connectivity, so lease duration does not explain the unreachable gateway.
answer_d_explanation: Correct. The host is in 192.168.40.64/26, while 192.168.40.1 is in a different /26 subnet.
reference_notes: Programmatic check: 192.168.40.70/26 is in 192.168.40.64 through .127. Usable addresses are .65 through .126. Gateway .1 is outside that subnet.
author_notes: Accelerated staging approval authorized by the repository owner on 2026-07-25.

objective_text: Given a scenario, troubleshoot common performance issues.
question_text: A small office has four nearby 2.4 GHz access points configured on channels 1, 4, 8, and 11. Users report high retransmission rates and inconsistent throughput. Which change is the best first step?
answer_a: Redesign the channel plan to use non-overlapping channels such as 1, 6, and 11, and move capable clients to 5 GHz where appropriate.
answer_b: Set every access point to maximum transmit power.
answer_c: Configure 40 MHz channels across the 2.4 GHz band.
answer_d: Assign a different SSID to every access point while retaining the same channels.
correct_explanation: Channels 4 and 8 overlap with nearby 2.4 GHz channels, which can increase contention and retransmissions. A non-overlapping plan and appropriate use of 5 GHz reduce co-channel and adjacent-channel interference.
answer_a_explanation: Correct. Channel planning directly addresses the overlap and can improve spectrum use.
answer_b_explanation: Increasing power on every AP can enlarge contention areas and make interference worse.
answer_c_explanation: Wider 2.4 GHz channels consume more of the limited band and can increase overlap.
answer_d_explanation: Changing SSIDs does not remove radio-frequency overlap or contention.
reference_notes: CompTIA objective 5.4 includes channel overlap, interference, and wireless performance. IEEE 802.11 defines wireless LAN operation.
author_notes: Accelerated staging approval authorized by the repository owner on 2026-07-25.

objective_text: Given a scenario, use the appropriate tool or protocol to solve networking issues.
question_text: Which command-line tool is used to display the sequence of Layer 3 hops toward a destination?
answer_a: ping
answer_b: traceroute or tracert
answer_c: nslookup
answer_d: cable tester
correct_explanation: Traceroute on many operating systems, or tracert on Windows, sends probes with increasing IP time-to-live values to reveal routers along the path toward a destination.
answer_a_explanation: Ping tests reachability and round-trip response but does not normally list each hop.
answer_b_explanation: Correct. Traceroute or tracert reveals the Layer 3 path hop by hop.
answer_c_explanation: Nslookup queries DNS and does not trace the routed path.
answer_d_explanation: A cable tester checks physical cabling and is not a command that discovers routed hops.
reference_notes: CompTIA objective 5.5 includes ping and traceroute. Traceroute behavior relies on IP TTL expiration and ICMP responses.
author_notes: Accelerated staging approval authorized by the repository owner on 2026-07-25.

objective_text: Given a scenario, troubleshoot common performance issues.
question_text: Ignoring protocol overhead, how long would it take to transmit 4 GB of data over a 1 Gbps link? Use decimal units: 1 GB equals 1,000,000,000 bytes and 1 Gbps equals 1,000,000,000 bits per second.
answer_a: 4 seconds
answer_b: 8 seconds
answer_c: 32 seconds
answer_d: 40 seconds
correct_explanation: Four gigabytes contains 32 gigabits because each byte contains 8 bits. Dividing 32 gigabits by 1 gigabit per second gives an ideal transmission time of 32 seconds. Real transfer time would be longer because the question excludes protocol and system overhead.
answer_a_explanation: This result treats bytes as bits and omits the factor of 8.
answer_b_explanation: This result does not account for all 4 GB of data at the stated bit rate.
answer_c_explanation: Correct. 4 GB multiplied by 8 equals 32 Gb, and 32 Gb divided by 1 Gbps equals 32 seconds.
answer_d_explanation: This adds time that is not supported by the stated ideal calculation.
reference_notes: Programmatic check using decimal units: 4,000,000,000 bytes multiplied by 8 divided by 1,000,000,000 bits per second equals 32 seconds.
author_notes: Accelerated staging approval authorized by the repository owner on 2026-07-25.
